title: Evangelist Pocket: Battle Lab Playlet (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
- Tiny, transportable slide pack (6–8 slides) for field evangelists and SEs to run a rapid 'battle lab' with platform/ML/infra buyers. Focus: surface operations risk, show fast canary plan, and leave with a measurable pilot hypothesis.

Target personas (primary -> secondary):
- Platform engineers (primary)
- ML infra / ML engineers (secondary)
- Product managers (risk/compliance lens)

Why this is different (one-liner):
- Not a full pilot playbook — this is a compact rebuttal + live experiment starter that gets teams to a yes/no pilot decision in a single working session.

Slide 1 — Opener (30s):
- Headline: "Ship LLM features faster without hidden ops tax"
- Subhead: 3 quick signals we surface in the session: latency ceiling, cost delta per 1k requests, fallback plan.
- Note to presenter: keep it energetic, set expectation that we’ll leave with a measurable pilot scope.

Slide 2 — Topline risks platform teams care about (visual list):
- Latency spikes on tail requests (p95/p99)
- Unpredictable per-token costs during bursts
- KV cache cold-starts for chat flows
- Model drift/regression after upgrades
- Compliance/data isolation for private data

Quick annotation (speaker note): call out one real example from customer repo — e.g., anonymized incident where an embedding job doubled token spend during retrain.

Slide 3 — The Battle Lab (30–45min workshop):
- Inputs we ask for: 1 representative request (prompt), approximate QPS distribution, target latency SLO, a small sample dataset (5–10 items).
- Fast experiments we run together:
  1) Latency profile baseline vs Redwood hosted variant (lightweight gen)
  2) Micro-batching demo: show effect on per-token latency and cost with same QPS
  3) Canary fallback plan: model variant + region + reserved pool toggle
- Output: 3 recommended actions and a pilot success metric (e.g., reduce 95th latency by X ms OR limit token spend to $Y per 1k calls).

Slide 4 — Live script + demo checklist (for SE):
- 0–5m: Gather inputs and define SLOs (write on board)
- 5–20m: Run quick gen test (we host a minimal harness) — note tok/sec and p95
- 20–30m: Flip batching/caching settings and re-run 
- 30–40m: Validate fallback plan and document rollout steps
- 40–45m: Agree next steps: pilot scope, timeline, responsible parties

Presenter cues: keep terminal/console visible, record the request IDs, timebox strictly.

Slide 5 — Objection playbook (rapid snippets):
- "We can build this ourselves": ask which parts they value (ops, perf, fallbacks) and offer a 4-week kill-switch pilot vs their internal PoC to compare TCO.
- "Costs will explode": show per-1k-call nominal numbers and impact of batching + prefix caching (two quick scenarios). Offer conservative reserved-capacity estimate.
- "Security/compliance": propose Private deployment handshake: VPC + retention controls + KMS anchor; offer a compliance checklist and timeline.
- "Model quality tradeoffs": show A/B guardrail: quality can be validated with held-out prompts; we default to higher-quality variant during canary.

Slide 6 — One-page pilot template (editable in session):
- Pilot name; success metric; duration (2–4 weeks); minimal acceptance criteria; rollback criteria; owner(s).
- Quick fields: estimated monthly token volume, suggested reserved capacity, baseline p95, target p95.

Practical scripts (copyable):
- 30s opener: "We run a 45-minute lab to get to a single pilot ask — usually a 2-week scope with measurable SLOs. If we don’t see a clear outcome, we walk away. No long procurement dance."
- Objection bite: "If you want to self-build, great — let’s still run the lab in parallel for 2 weeks and compare unit economics and ops overhead."

Evidence snippets (to swap in slide or appendix):
- Microcase: consumer SaaS company reduced median token cost 28% by adopting prefix caching + batching; p95 latency improved 18% after small config tweaks. (anonymized)
- Operations: example rollback plan we executed for a canary that regressed quality — automatic fallback to 1.1 variant + traffic steering to reserved pool.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Add short graph templates: cost per-1k baseline vs batching vs cached scenario (need numbers from analytics team).
- Pull two anonymized customer before/after charts (ask CS: Marisol).
- Create a 1‑pager compliance checklist for Private deployment with SRE.

Call to action for SE / field:
- Run this with 3 target accounts next quarter (booked as 45m sessions). Measure: pilot conversion rate and time-to-pilot.

Appendix (optional slides we swap in depending on audience):
- Quick kernel: how batching interacts with latency at low QPS
- Cost math worked example for embeddings vs chat vs rerank
- Template canary policy (YAML snippet) and guardrails (who can flip, who must approve)

Notes: keep language punchy, avoid heavy slides. The goal is to create urgency and leave with a clear pilot scope.

Linked resources (presenter cheat links):
- Canary checklist: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Canary+Checklist
- Pilot template (Google sheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1PilotTemplate
- Recorder: use the SE lab harness (internal link) to capture perf results quickly

Action items after session:
- Upload sample prompts + perf logs to pilot tracker (tag: pilot-evangelist)
- Draft pilot SOW and circulate to PM + SRE for sign-off within 48 hours

Questions for review in GTM sync:
- Which slide variant lands best with platform engineers: cost-first vs latency-first? (A/B test idea)
- Can we get a minimal analytics export to populate the cost graphs automatically?

Last thought (keep this tone in deck):
- We’re running a lab, not a bake-off. Make it clear that the goal is a decision with a metric, not a month-long demo run.

(End of draft — rough slide text + speaker notes; needs perf numbers and 2 anonymized charts. Drop-in content for SEs in the field.)
